question: In Python, an if-statement must always include an else clause.
The condition in a Python if-statement must evaluate to a Boolean value (True or False).
Indentation is used in Python to define the block of code that belongs to an if-statement.
A Python if-statement can only evaluate a single condition and cannot handle multiple conditions.
In Python, the elif clause must directly follow an if statement and precede an else clause if one is present.
In Python, the colon (:) after the condition in an if-statement is optional.
In a nested if-statement, the inner if-statement is only executed if the outer if-statement's condition is True.
Python's if statements do not support the use of ternary conditional operators.
If an exception is raised in the condition of an if-statement, the else clause will still execute.
In Python, an if statement can exist without an else or elif clause, but an elif clause cannot appear without a preceding if statement.
